title: mcmt edit plan
description: Layer 5 (output backend) output, consumed by the writer. Kept as a separate contract so the output backend stays decoupled from the writer (an architectural requirement, not a staffing one) and so each layer has its own regression fixture. A backend decides WHAT value goes where; the writer decides HOW to encode it, and owns NBT list homogeneity, surgical region rewriting, backups and rollback.

backend.description: v1 ships resourcepack only. The inplace value exists so the pluggable-backend seam is real rather than hypothetical; nothing emits it yet.

world_fingerprint.description: Re-derived from the live world at apply time. A mismatch means the world moved under the plan -- most often because someone simply opened it in-game, which upgrades chunk DataVersions.

assets.description: Files the backend produced that apply must place into the world folder. Paths are relative to the run's output directory.

unwritten.description: Units the BACKEND declined to write. Refusals originating in the writer go to apply_report.unwritten instead, with their own reason vocabulary.

container.description: Copied verbatim from the occurrence. The writer uses container.data_version only to decide what generation to write the CHUNK back as; the node encoding comes from expected_encoding.

expected_encoding.description: The encoding recorded at scan time. Required, not optional: the writer re-reads the node and aborts the ENTIRE plan if it no longer matches, so a stale plan can never half-apply.

allOf.description: A legacy JSON-shaped node inside a chunk that the game will NOT run DataFixerUpper on (data_version >= 4325) is display garbage, not content. [遊戲實測 M0-3/M0-4] Writing a translated JSON string back there produces a node that still renders as literal braces and quotes. Extract marks such occurrences excluded; this rule makes it structurally impossible for a backend to emit one anyway.

oneOf.description: Collapse the whole node to one translate component. Only legal when the unit is collapsible.

style.description: Formatting to place on the new component. Derived from the occurrence's segment_styles, not blindly copied.

oneOf.description: Write a literal string INTO THE NODE, keeping the node's existing NBT shape. A plain_string or bare_string node gets a bare string back; a text_compound node gets {"text": ...}; an empty_key_compound node gets {"": ...} -- the writer never normalises one compound shape into the other, because that would re-encode a node nobody asked it to change. The shape comes from expected_encoding, which the writer re-checks against the node before writing. It deliberately does NOT promote a TAG_String into a compound: [遊戲實測 M11-3] the field that forced this path, CustomName in a native chunk, renders whatever string is there literally, and promoting it has never been tested.

text.description: Final text with formatting codes already reinstated. A surviving [[n]] token is a bug: the writer MUST reject the plan rather than write it.

oneOf.description: Rebuild a non-collapsible component tree. Emitted when unit.collapsible is false, i.e. the tree carries click_event / hover_event / font / insertion / nested translate, or styling that legacy § codes cannot express. The backend fills each text slot with a per-segment translate key derived as <unit.key>.<segment_index>.

tree.description: The component tree to write, built from occurrence.skeleton with each segment slot filled in. Shape mirrors a Minecraft text component.
